findings.title: Generated profile-root pin and zero-write budget conflict with the genuine original CLI
findings.evidence: prepareProfile always writeFileSyncs the genuine public PROFILE_ROOT_CONFIG on every ordinary CLI start. That literal is 223 UTF-8 bytes, SHA256 c300dcf2ebc5f02062d6591268d29d3db6fe45e0cb138f5467276fe2ba06076e. Both r2 lifecycle templates instead pin the historical 68-byte preparation-source root, SHA256 752d0dd14f655a392c55432801ceb46909f1d593bae640e05fae949fba970e70. The plan budgets zero profile-config writes and claims unchanged config.
findings.impact: An already booted canonical generated root cannot satisfy the historical preparation pin. Starting from that preparation copy would let the original CLI replace its bytes, contradicting the unchanged-file/effect claim. This is a source contradiction; this auditor did not inspect the active root or perform a failed launch.
findings.requiredRemediation: Preserve r2 intact. Seal a successor that pins the genuine compiled public root before/after, distinguishes generated-root rewrites from user package/patch/settings changes, and records one automatic generated-root write per normal start and one additional write for conditional rollback. Root must freshly compare only the public generated-root metadata/bytes under the explicitly authorized scope before any lifecycle operation.

findings.title: Multiple failure/signal paths can escalate original shutdown
findings.evidence: failClosed sends SIGTERM without a stop latch. Both private log streams independently call it; root SIGINT/SIGTERM forwarding independently sends another child signal. Genuine createProcessShutdown.interrupt escalates a repeated signal to immediate process exit.
findings.impact: Two log errors, or a log failure plus owner cleanup, can defeat the original single-signal disposal grace. A PTY/process-group signal must also not reach both wrapper and child while the wrapper forwards it. The one-owned-stop/no-force-escalation plan is therefore unproven on the r2 literal.
findings.requiredRemediation: Seal a successor with one common child-stop latch across IO errors and root signals, preserve failed exit status, and refuse child spawn after pre-spawn IO failure. Root must signal only a freshly identified owned wrapper parent PID once, not an unknown PTY/process group; verify current parent/child/executable/source/listener identity. A successor should report its wrapper PID for this check. Let original five-second disposal grace and bounded root observation finish; no second signal, force kill or alternate port.
